title: Thermometer (part 3)
textbookText: Good to Know: 1. During the heating of a matter, it undergoes either change of temperature or change of state, but not both at a time. During the change of temperature, the state of matter remains unchanged and vice versa. 2. During the process of melting, the solid and the liquid states of matter co-exist in thermal equilibrium. During the process of boiling, the liquid and the gas states of matter coexist in thermal equilibrium. During the process of sublimation, the solid and the gaseous states of matter coexist in thermal equilibrium. 3. The water at 100C is better than the water at 0C for extinguishing fire. 4. Specific heat capacity has different values for different states of the same matter. Water has the specific heat of 4200 J kg–1K–1but that of ice is 2100 J kg–1K–1. 5. In the heat-temperature graph, the horizontal portion of solid melting is shorter than that of liquid boiling. It is not accidental. The latent heat of vaporization is greater than the latent heat of fusion. 6. In the heat-temperature graph, the slope of the line for solid warming, liquid warming, and gas warming are different for the same matter indicating different values of specific heat for different states. Again, the slope for each line has a different value for different matter indicating that the specific heat capacity depends on the nature of a material.

11.13 Determination of Specific Latent Heat of Fusion of Ice by the Method of Mixture
The specific latent heat of the fusion of ice is defined as the heat required to change the state of a unit mass of ice into water at its melting point.
Using principle of calorimetry, we can determine the specific latent heat of the fusion of ice from the method of mixture.
